Theorem 1: 'Given gamma_1>0, gamma_k=(-a)^k/2, a in (0,1/n), k>1, the attention matrix Ahat in ParaFormer is a polynomial graph filter'. Ahat = Softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d)) -- NON-NEGATIVE base. Distinct ParaFormers also exist: 2206.08317, 2303.00941, 2409.17746, 2412.16763, 2510.15425.

text: DERIVED from results/s2.jsonl, no new run: pivot_unsigned__at_pivots reads 0.0 at s=8/32/128/512 (0/4096 each). That is NOT a measurement of the S2 ablation, it is the semiring theorem restated. With out = v + Av + A^2 v the influence Jacobian wrt v is I+A+A^2, non-negative entrywise for non-negative A, so a softmax-routed arm CANNOT flip sign on the v-path at any s. The unsigned ablation is ZERO BY CONSTRUCTION on wrt='v' -- the exact defect that made M2 kill clause 2 unevaluable (instrument #15). G4 / CHECKLIST S2 can only be decided on wrt='x'.

DERIVED from results/s2.jsonl wrt='x', no new run: unsigned/signed log-log slopes over s=8..32 are -1.4281 and +0.2025; the two curves CROSS at s = 18.4. Unsigned is 3.889x BETTER than signed at s=8 (0.1025391 vs 0.0263672), 2.466x WORSE at s=32, 20.4x worse at s=128, and 0/4096 by s=512. The published '>=42.7x at s=512' separation is 0.03125 divided by the ONE-SIDED 95% Clopper-Pearson upper on 0/4096 = 0.00073111; the TWO-SIDED 97.5% upper is 0.00090020, giving 34.7x. Both bounds should be stated, not one.

COSTING, not a claim: scale/negation_scope.py is a COMPLETE M3 instrument whose absolute bar is already RED-tested (results/iter04_m3_bar_calibration.txt: predict_the_mean 1.000000, payload_only 1.414204, oracle 0.000000). It has NO ARMS -- no softmax arm, no pivot arm, bootstrap_ci has zero callers (house-events.jsonl:1926, Chase RED). The gap between M2's statistic and M3's capability is a readout head and an Adam loop, not a GPU. Nobody in this project has ever timed a training run on this CPU.

DERIVED, structural: NEITHER placement can decide the claim on its own. wrt='v' (results/m2.jsonl) has the routing comparison -- pivot_signed vs dense_signed -- but its signedness ablation pivot_unsigned__at_pivots is 0.0 by the semiring theorem, so signedness is untestable there. wrt='x' (results/s2.jsonl) has the signedness comparison -- pivot_signed__x vs pivot_unsigned__x -- but has NO dense control at all, so routing is untestable there. The claim sentence needs BOTH legs and no single placement supplies both. A dense_signed__x arm is the missing cell.

RECOMPUTED from results/s2.jsonl. (a) unsigned x-decay '-1.598, R2 0.9962' REPRODUCES EXACTLY -- but only over s=8..128, the three NONZERO points; s=512 is 0/4096 and cannot be logged. The decay is therefore fit over a 16x range, not the 64x it reads as. Substituting the one-sided CP upper for the zero gives -1.2466, R2 0.9474 over the full 8..512. Both should be stated. (b) I could NOT reproduce 'signed holds -0.021'; least-squares log-log over the same four points gives +0.0124 with R2 = 0.0204. R2 of 0.02 means the SIGN of that slope is not determined by the data. Both readings agree the arm is flat; neither licenses a signed slope value.

R5 PRE-REGISTRATION FROZEN. Appended to DONE.md BEFORE any R5 number existed (arm-building nurse still running, zero results seen). LOCK R5 d8491f67bf6b. Four kill clauses K1-K4, each with its structural-fire argument. K3 is the one that inherits instrument #15: on a v-path readout the unsigned ablation is 0 by the semiring theorem (results/s2.jsonl, 0/4096 at s=8/32/128/512) and CANNOT fire; it is evaluable only on an x-path readout, where unsigned reads 0.1025390625 at s=8. K4 exists because float('nan') >= 1.0 is False in Python.

CREDIT WHERE DUE, then a discrepancy. scale/pivot_probe.py:184-193 ALREADY documents in code what I derived independently: the v-path unsigned arm is 'vacuous, not a win' and x is 'the only channel on which signed-routed vs unsigned-routed is a real comparison'. So the S2/G4 defect was known to whoever wrote that comment. BUT the same comment cites 'the repo's record: 0.025391 / 0.009766 / 0.000000' for softmax on wrt='x' at s=8/32/128, and results/s2.jsonl reads 0.102539 / 0.014160 / 0.001221 for pivot_unsigned__x at the same sizes. 13/512 vs 420/4096 -- a 4x disagreement at s=8, far outside binomial noise. Probable cause: different arms (dense hop2 A@A vs pivot hop2 A[:,P]@A[P,:]) at different draw counts, but README.md:232 and pivot_probe.py:192 cite them interchangeably as 'softmax'. NOT called a bug; called UNRECONCILED. The load-bearing 'unsigned is ~4x better at s=8' rests on whichever of the two is the right arm, and nobody has said which.

CONSEQUENCE of the above: the wrt='x' channel has NO dense control of either sign at 4096 draws. results/s2.jsonl holds only pivot_signed__x and pivot_unsigned__x. So on the only channel where signedness is testable, ROUTING is untested; and on the channel where routing is tested (wrt='v', results/m2.jsonl), signedness is vacuous. Two arms are missing from the 2x2: dense_signed__x and dense_unsigned__x at matched n.

text: INSTRUMENT #15 IS ALIVE AND UNFIXED, in a sibling of the function that was patched. scale/m2_units.py:316 reads `k2 = (b > -0.3) if b == b else False`. That is character-for-character the bug that _verdict()'s own docstring (m2_units.py:234-236) says was ELIMINATED. b is slope(pivot_signed__not_in_P), which is NaN because loglog_slope (pivot_probe.py:70-72) returns nan when fewer than 2 points have y>0, and not_in_P is 0/4096 at every size. So NaN -> k2=False -> line 320 prints 'control decays as the mechanism requires' -> line 322 prints M2 = GREEN. tests/chase/test_m2_verdict_nan.py imports only _verdict, never report(), so nothing catches it. THE FIXED FUNCTION IS NOT THE ONE THE FULL VERDICT PATH CALLS. m2_units.py is on my do-not-touch list; reporting, not fixing.

WORSE THAN A FALSE GREEN: scale/s2_units.py:131-139. sl from loglog_slope can be NaN; `nan > -0.3` is False at line 131, so control falls to the else at 136 and PRINTS 'unsigned routing DECAYS (slope nan) while signed routing is flat (+0.0270) -- signedness is load-bearing ON TOP of routing, and that combination is the unoccupied cell.' That is the strongest sentence in the project, emitted for an undefined slope. grep -rn s2_units tests/ = zero hits; no test exercises this branch. s2_units.py is on my do-not-touch list; reporting, not fixing.

M3's THREE KILL CLAUSES CANNOT FIRE TODAY -- none of the three quantities is computed by any code in the repo. negation_scope.main() calls only calibrate_bar; bootstrap_ci has zero callers; no unsigned-arm NRMSE exists anywhere. tests/chase/test_checklist_kills_are_evaluable.py runs 5 FAILED / 1 PASSED, and the one that passes (test_g4_has_an_evaluator) passes because its evaluator is s2_units.report -- the site with the NaN defect above. CAVEAT I AM PUTTING ON MY OWN NUMBER. tests/chase/test_m2_instrument_binds.py reports 4 of 5 FAILED, including '|P| = 6 not 8 at s=8' and 's=8 pivot/dense cells are bitwise-identical'. results/m2.jsonl confirms the latter: pivot_signed__in_P/s8 and dense_signed__at_pivots/s8 both read exactly 0.024658203125. So at s=8 the pivot restriction is nearly vacuous (6 pivots over at most 7 causal rows). My DERIVED crossover of s=18.4 between signed and unsigned on wrt='x' is anchored on the s=8 endpoint and is therefore SOFT. The bracket that survives is measured, not fitted: unsigned is above signed at s=8 and below it at s=32, so the crossover lies in [8,32]. The value 18.4 should be quoted as an interpolation, never as a measurement.

THE TRADEOFF REFUSED, WITH ARITHMETIC. [RUN, my own probe, 20 torch threads, CPU] one fwd+bwd of the M3 shape (causal signed op + pivot hop2 + readout, d_model=16, k=8) costs 146.1 ms/step at n=128 s=260, so 616 steps fit in a 90 s bucket; 275.9 ms at n=256 s=260; 482.1 ms at n=128 s=512; 1605.2 ms at n=256 s=512. Warm-up step excluded and DECLARED; 5-step median; no optimizer, no eval, no bootstrap, so this is a LOWER BOUND on a full arm, not the arm cost. A 3-arm 500-step comparison at s=260/d=256 is ~3 buckets, ~220 s. [DERIVED from meta.seconds in results/m2.jsonl + results/s2.jsonl] the statistic already cost 4895.8 s + 1558.2 s = 6454.0 s = 107.6 min of this same CPU, of which 5049.4 s = 84.2 min is the s>=1024 columns alone. So the CAPABILITY route is roughly 3% of what the STATISTIC route has already spent. The premise that the decisive route is the expensive one is false on this box.

INSTRUMENT #15, THIRD INSTANCE -- AND IT IS IN M4, A MANDATORY CHECKLIST CELL. [RUN] `python -m pytest tests/chase/test_checklist_kills_are_evaluable.py -x -q -k m4` -> 1 failed in 1.41s. AssertionError: 'the perturbed token was outside `keep` in all 8 draws' (assert 0 > 0), tests/chase/test_checklist_kills_are_evaluable.py:104. The mechanism is in the call signature itself: ev.lowest_salience_token(x, RHO, exclude=keep) EXCLUDES the keep set, so the token that gets perturbed can never be inside keep, so the measured movement of kept content is 0.000000e+00 BY CONSTRUCTION. M4's kill is 'max change > 1e-12'; that quantity is never nonzero, so M4's kill CANNOT FIRE. The headline 'do(c) measured at 0.000000e+00 for eviction against 2.154868e-05 for post-softmax gating' (CHECKLIST.md:153,182; README.md:825,853) is therefore not a comparison of two operators -- one side is a structural constant. This also removes M4 as the zero-training fallback capability I was about to nominate.

CORRECTION TO A NUMBER I WAS GIVEN AND WOULD HAVE REPEATED. BLiMP sentential_negation_npi_scope, arXiv:1912.00582v4 Table 4, extracted from the PDF with pypdf: '5-gram 45, LSTM 23, TXL 53, GPT-2 73, Human 81'. My brief carried GPT-2 = 95. IT IS 73. Four of the five anchors were correct, which is exactly what made the fifth easy to miss -- the same internally-consistent-externally-wrong pattern that produced fifteen instrument failures here. Consequence: the paradigm is NOT saturated. GPT-2-large is 774M params and sits 8 points BELOW the human 81, and Transformer-XL (103M params, 103M training tokens) reads 53. A 25.7M model has a real band to land in, and the honest target for a small-data run is TXL's 53, not a near-ceiling 95.

BabyLM STRICT-SMALL IS THE WRONG TRACK FOR THIS MODEL, with arithmetic. Strict-Small = 9.96M WORDS (arXiv:2504.08165 Table 1, 'Total - 9.96M 98.04M 100%'); Strict = 98.04M words. This project's tokenizer is byte-level (vocab_size=256, ceq/hf/train.py DEFAULTS), so 9.96M words x 5-6 bytes = 49.8-59.8M byte-tokens. Chinchilla for 25,182,208 non-embedding params at 20 tok/param = 503,644,160 tokens. Strict-Small is SHORT BY 8.4x-10.1x and would need 8.4-10.1 epochs; Strict is 490-588M tokens = 97-117% of the budget. Also verified independently: instantiating ceq/hf/train.py DEFAULTS reproduces 25,707,520 params exactly (25,182,208 non-embedding + 131,072 + 262,144 + 1,024 + 131,072). Also: arXiv:2404.06214 is the 2nd-challenge CALL FOR PAPERS, not a findings paper -- it has no corpus table. The findings papers are 2504.08165 and 2412.05149.

BLiMP EVALUATION IS ALMOST FREE, and that is what makes it a candidate. Protocol (arXiv:1912.00582): zero-shot minimal-pair likelihood comparison, no fine-tuning, no generation -- 'observing whether they assign a higher probability to the acceptable sentence'. 1,000 pairs per paradigm, so sentential_negation_npi_scope is 2,000 forward passes. At 2*N*tokens forward-only with ~71 byte-tokens/sentence: 7.301e12 FLOPs = 73-730 CPU-seconds depending on assumed throughput (10/50/100 GFLOPS, ESTIMATE, not sourced). The full 67-paradigm suite is ~67x that. The COST IS ALL IN THE PRETRAINING, none in the eval. ALSO NOTE: arXiv:2504.08165 reports NO wall-clock and NO GPU type for any BabyLM baseline or entrant -- grepped, zero hits. There is no published compute figure to compare against.

REFINING MY OWN M4 FINDING -- being precise, because the loose version overstates it. [READ] tests/w3/test_w3_eviction.py:84-92: BOTH arms perturb the SAME token (`crushed`, chosen with exclude=keep) and compare settle_gated vs settle_evicted on the same edit. So the eviction-vs-gating comparison IS symmetric and fair, and the gating leak of 2.154868e-05 is a real measurement. What is NOT a measurement is the eviction side: the crushed token is excluded from keep, so settle_evicted drops it entirely, so editing it cannot move kept rows -- 0.000000e+00 is 'you deleted it, so it stopped mattering', a tautology. The defect is in the KILL, not the comparison: CHECKLIST M4's kill reads 'max change > 1e-12' about SETTLED STATE OF UNRELATED CONTENT, i.e. content inside keep, and tests/chase/test_checklist_kills_are_evaluable.py:104 shows the perturbed token was outside keep in 8 of 8 draws (assert 0 > 0, FAILED). So the M4 kill is written about kept content and measured on deleted content, and it cannot fire. Corrected reading: M4's claim survives as a systems statement (exact retraction), but its pre-registered kill is unevaluable as coded.

R5 LEARNABILITY CONTROL -- RUN, and it is the control R5 needs before any arm is credited. [RUN, CPU, 20 threads] M3 negation-scope at s=260, d=256 (flipper@3, payload@258, query@259), n_train=1024, held-out batch generated with a DIFFERENT seed (999 vs 0). An ORACLE-GATHER model -- routing handed over for free, 6,337 params, only the multiplicative combination learned -- reads: steps=0 heldout 1.0009 [ABOVE BAR], steps=100 heldout 0.0478, steps=300 heldout 0.0139, steps=500 heldout 0.0071, in 3.86 SECONDS total for the 500-step run. TWO THINGS THIS ESTABLISHES. (1) RED-FIRST FIRES: the untrained model reads 1.0009, above the predict-the-mean bar of 1.0, so K1 can reach both sides of its threshold -- unlike M2 clause 2 and unlike the M4 kill. (2) The readout+MLP+Adam budget SOLVES this task in under 4 seconds when routing is free, so any arm failure at d=256 is attributable to ROUTING and not to the training budget. The oracle-routed upper bound is 0.0071 against a predict-the-mean 1.0; that is the band the arms have to land in.

THE 25,707,520 FIGURE IS WRONG BY 20,480 AND THE CAUSE IS A BUG IN sizing.py. [RUN] building the notebook's exact object via ceq.hf.train.build(**dict(ceq_train.DEFAULTS)) and summing p.numel() gives 25,728,000, not 25,707,520. [READ] ceq/sizing.py:128-140 `per_layer = (3*d*d + d*d) + (d*f + f*d) + 4*d` counts qkv/o_proj correctly as bias-free (modeling_ceq.py:393-394 use bias=False) but the MLP at modeling_ceq.py:419 is nn.Linear(d,f) / nn.Linear(f,d) with PyTorch's DEFAULT bias=True, and sizing.params() never adds those bias vectors. 8 layers x (2048+512) = 20,480, matching the diff EXACTLY. Magnitude 0.08% -- does not move the T4 memory conclusion (preflight reproduces README's 2.72 GiB / 13.50 GiB budget / +10.78 GiB headroom) -- but it is the arithmetic every scaling claim in this project is built on.

THE 1.6% CHINCHILLA CLAIM HOLDS UNDER EVERY CONVENTION. [RUN] notebook ships steps=2000 (colab/train_ceq.ipynb:191), batch=8, seq=512 (ceq/hf/train.py:45-46) = 8,192,000 tokens. Against 20*N: 1.593% at the claimed 25,707,520, 1.592% at the measured 25,728,000, 1.627% at sizing.py's own non-embedding convention of 25,182,208 (TOKENS_PER_PARAM=20 at sizing.py:275, chinchilla_tokens uses non-embedding at sizing.py:289-290). All three round to 1.6%. The 300M pricing also reproduces from code: CFG_300M non-embedding 302,088,192, h_softmax 41.4/46.8 A100-h, h_sgate 129.7/257.2 A100-h at seq 1024/2048 -- NOT fabricated in prose.

CAVEAT ON A NUMBER MY OWN NURSE PRODUCED, and the contamination is MINE. The 25.7M model was timed on this CPU at min 4454.2 ms/step, median 6799.9 ms/step, batch 8 seq 512, 20 torch threads. Steps 2-4 climbed from 6.8s to 9.3s -- I was running my own R5 cost probe and the M3 learnability control on the same box at the same time. Treat 4454.2 ms as the best-case and the median as contaminated BY ME. Separately: the two T4 extrapolations DISAGREE BY 4-9x -- 6ND at 65 TFLOPS and 25-40% MFU gives 24-39 ms/step, while measured-CPU divided by an UNVERIFIED 20-40x speedup guess gives 111-223 ms/step. Neither is a T4 measurement and neither should be quoted as one. Also worth knowing: ceq/sizing.py:304-307's own docstring says gpu_hours() is 'only meaningful for the SOFTMAX arm'; the sgate cost is the softmax number times MEASURED_STEP_RATIO = {1024: 3.13, 2048: 5.49}, a hardcoded dict at tests/chase/test_scale_sizing.py:494 measured on an RTX 4060 Laptop, not on an A100.

NEW MEASUREMENT, one bucket, 40.8 s total, no file written to results/. Ran scale.pivot_probe.run_arm at the SHIPPED protocol (n_draws=4096, k=8, placement='in_P', seed=0, protocol='SCALING', wrt='x') at the missing size s=16. pivot_unsigned__x/s16 = 174/4096 = 0.042480469, CP95 [0.036510, 0.049114], 18.5 s. pivot_signed__x/s16 = 119/4096 = 0.029052734, CP95 [0.024125, 0.034666], 22.3 s. THE INTERVALS DO NOT OVERLAP: at s=16 the UNSIGNED arm is significantly BETTER than the signed one. Combined with unsigned 0.014160 vs signed 0.034912 at s=32, the crossover is bracketed by MEASUREMENT in (16, 32) and interpolates to s = 19.6 (log-log slopes over 16..32: unsigned -1.5850, signed +0.2651). This replaces my earlier s=18.4, which was anchored on s=8 where |P|=6 makes the pivot restriction nearly vacuous. The bracket is now measured on a size where that objection does not apply, and the answer barely moved. STANDING CONSEQUENCE: 'softmax cannot do this' is false below roughly twenty tokens of context, with non-overlapping intervals saying so.

SECOND CORRECTION TO MY OWN BRIEF. 'TinyStories publishes GPT-4-graded scores at 1M/2.5M/8.3M/28M' is TRUE only of ANECDOTES. arXiv:2305.07759 Figures 6, 7 and 8 are SINGLE-PROMPT, SINGLE-SCORE examples (e.g. 28M reads Grammar/Creativity/Consistency 9/6/9 on the 'ladder' prompt, 9/7/9 on 'pumpkin', 8/5/8 on 'black cat'; 1M reads 6/3/2, 4/4/3, 2/1/1). The paper's ACTUAL benchmark protocol is Section 3: '~50 prompts', '10 completions with temperature 1', averaged -- and that averaged result appears ONLY in Figure 4, a bar-chart IMAGE keyed by hidden-size x layer-count, NOT by the four round parameter labels. There is no text table of averaged scores at 1M/2.5M/8.3M/28M. Anyone citing those four as a benchmark is citing three anecdotes. Also: the paper's largest sweep point is ~80M ('almost perfect scores in terms of grammar and consistency'), not 28M.

TINYSTORIES PARAMETER BRANDING DOES NOT SURVIVE A COUNT. Instantiating each live HuggingFace config.json as GPTNeoForCausalLM: TinyStories-1M has 3,745,984 parameters at its config's literal vocab_size=50257. Re-counting at vocab_size=10000 (the paper's stated 'top 10K most common tokens') gives 1,169,536 / 3,125,504 / 9,396,736 / 31,376,384 / 37,596,672 / 24,932,352 for the six checkpoints. The paper's footnote 2 says the models are '1M/3M/9M/28M/33M'; the live repo says '1M/3M/8M/28M/33M'; the prose says 8.3M. UNVERIFIED which convention the branding counts. CONSEQUENCE FOR BRACKETING: this project's 3,652,096-param run is bracketed by (2.5M, 8.3M) and the 25.7M notebook default by (8.3M, 28M) -- TWO DIFFERENT PAIRS, not one. And every TinyStories checkpoint uses a 50,257 BPE vocab while this project is byte-level (vocab 256), so parameter-count bracketing does not imply comparability.

TINYSTORIES COSTED. Dataset: 2,141,709 rows, TinyStories-train.txt = 1,924,281,556 bytes (HTTP HEAD on the CDN). Token count is NOT stated in the paper; measured by tokenizing a real 20MB sample with tiktoken gpt2 = 4.098 bytes/token, giving ~469.6M tokens as a LOWER BOUND (the paper's 10K-vocab restriction splits rare words further, so the true count is higher). Training 25.7M params on one epoch: 6*N*D = 7.2432e16 FLOPs; on a T4 at 65 TFLOPS fp16 (nvidia.com spec, quoted) at 10/20/30% MFU = 3.10 / 1.55 / 1.03 hours. FITS A 12-HOUR SESSION WITH ROOM FOR THREE EPOCHS at the pessimistic MFU. Paper's own hardware statement, Section 4 verbatim: 'All of the models can be trained on a single V100 GPU within at most 30 hours.' GRADING IS NOT FREE: 50 prompts x 10 completions = 500 GPT-4 calls, measured at 389 input / 73 output tokens per call from the paper's own worked example = $8.03 on gpt-4-0613, $0.68 on gpt-4.1. THE FREE SUBSTITUTE EXISTS AND THE PAPER USES IT: held-out cross-entropy on TinyStories-valid.txt, which Section 3.1 says tracks the GPT-4 scores -- but the correlation is stated QUALITATIVELY ONLY, with no regression and no mapping, so it cannot be converted into a graded score. No eval harness was ever released; only Evaluation_prompts.yaml (45 entries).

text: THE MISSING ARM IS MEASURED AND IT GOES AGAINST THE ROUTING STORY AT SMALL s. [RUN, 143.9 s total, shipped protocol n_draws=4096 k=8 placement=in_P seed=0 SCALING wrt='x', nothing written to results/] dense_signed__x: s=8 243/4096 = 0.059326172 CP95[0.052286,0.067003]; s=16 190/4096 = 0.046386719 CP95[0.040149,0.053281]; s=32 169/4096 = 0.041259766 CP95[0.035376,0.047809]. Against pivot_signed__x re-measured in the same process: 0.026367188 CP95[0.021679,0.031747] / 0.029052734 CP95[0.024125,0.034666] / 0.034912109 CP95[0.029503,0.040997] -- and the s=8 and s=32 values REPRODUCE results/s2.jsonl BIT-FOR-BIT, so the instrument did not move. VERDICT: on the representation path DENSE BEATS PIVOT AT EVERY SIZE MEASURED, with NON-OVERLAPPING intervals at s=8 and s=16. Routing does not buy anything below s=32 on this channel. Log-log slopes over 8..32: dense -0.2620, pivot +0.2025 -- dense decays only a third as fast as it does on the v-path (-0.746), and the two curves CONVERGE rather than separate.

PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTION, WRITTEN BEFORE THE RUN. Extrapolating the two log-log fits above, pivot_signed__x overtakes dense_signed__x at s = 46. The cheapest possible test is ONE size: s=64, both arms, same protocol, ~100 s of CPU. THE READING IS FIXED NOW. (A) pivot > dense at s=64 with non-overlapping CP95 -> routing is vindicated on the representation path and the convergence at s<=32 is a small-s artifact. (B) intervals OVERLAP at s=64 -> the crossover is real but slower than fitted; report the overlap, do not round it into a win. (C) dense STILL above pivot at s=64 with non-overlapping CP95 -> the extrapolation is wrong, routing does not help on the representation path in the measured range, and the claim sentence may not say routing holds signed influence flat WITHOUT naming the channel it fails on. I am running it next; this text does not get edited afterwards.

M2' R1-R4 are ONE mechanism. On the SAME 512 draws at s=128/512, R2's sign-determinacy predicate PARTITIONS M2's flip statistic: flip|determined 0.0068 CP[0.0014,0.0199] vs flip|undetermined 0.1622 CP[0.0867,0.2661], intervals disjoint, 24x. R2 GREEN IS M2's flip rate going to zero.

R2's determined fraction is a DOMINANCE TEST ON THE ONE-HOP EDGE, not a sign-structure test. Closed form: determined iff |A[i,j]| >= the one-sided pivot mass. Measured D_block 0.8555/0.8438 at s=128/512 while all-signs-agree is only 0.0215/0.0508. The 10^4 resamples reproduce the closed form exactly and buy nothing; at s=512 they OVER-report determinacy 55/64 vs the exact 53/64.

THE TWIN TEST: on |A| (scale/s2_probe.py absmag, magnitudes bit-identical, signs stripped) R2's determined fraction is 1.0000 and R3's balanced-ambiguity is exactly 0.0000 at s=128 and s=512, n=512. Both criteria are maximally passed by an operator with NO SIGNS. Neither can be evidence for signed influence.

R1's kill cannot fire: perturbing an off-support token moves the pivot readout by 0.000e+00, 96/96 bitwise identical at s=128 and s=512. Same structural zero as M2 clause 2. On dense_signed the same probe reads 8.795e-02 / 5.201e-02, so the kill fires only if the pivot mechanism is abandoned.

R4's theta saturates: k=8*s^theta clipped at s-3 makes theta=0.7 and theta=1.0 the IDENTICAL arm at s=32/128/512 (k=29/125/509), and slope(theta) is NaN at theta>=0.7 because the rate hits exactly 0. A crossing cannot be located where the parameter is non-injective and the function undefined. Instrument #15's NaN-slope-read-as-GREEN, rebuilt.

ROOT CAUSE, one sentence: all four M2' routes are thresholds on ONE scalar -- the intervened token's two-hop path weight against the one-hop offset and the background spread -- which is sign-blind (measured) and degree-1 homogeneous under per-row rescale (the rescale lemma), so no one of them can distinguish signed influence from magnitude bookkeeping.

R5 COST CORRECTION -- THE PIVOT ARM IS BOTTLENECKED BY A PYTHON LOOP, NOT BY THE OPERATOR. [READ] scale/m3_capability.py:100-107: hop2 = torch.stack([pivot_hop2(a[i], select_pivots(k[i], k_pivots)) for i in range(n)], dim=0). Pivots are content-selected per example, and pivot_hop2 only accepts a single 2D [s,s] operator, so the forward pass runs n Python-level iterations per step. [RUN] at n_train=1024, s=64, d=24, 150 steps: softmax finished in 17.1 s; the two pivot arms did not finish in over 8 minutes on the same data. My own shape probe using a SHARED pivot set taken from batch element 0 ran the same operator at 146.1 ms/step at n=128, s=260. So the gap is the loop, and it is vectorizable (batched gather + bmm). ANYONE COSTING R5 SHOULD PRICE THE VECTORIZED FORM, NOT THIS ONE.

THE ORDERING IS STABLE AND MEANINGFUL -- pivot_signed beats softmax with non-overlapping CIs in every run, and pivot_unsigned sits on top of softmax, which is the S2 decomposition M2 could never produce -- BUT THE ORDERING IS BELOW THE BAR ONLY IN THE SENSE THAT EVERY ARM FAILS IT. On the pre-registered kill, K1 FIRES on every configuration run so far. Two things are NOT yet established and must not be assumed: no arm has been run at d >= 256 to completion, and the pivot arms have not been run at n_train=1024 to completion. R5 is not GREEN, it is not RED, it is PARTIALLY RUN, and the part that has run says the arms do not clear the absolute bar.

THE SUCCESSOR, NAMED IN ADVANCE AS THE STANDING ORDER REQUIRES. If K1 holds at d >= 256 once the pivot arms are vectorised and run, R5 does not leave the project with nothing -- the successor is TinyStories at the 25.7M notebook default, and it is costed: 6*N*D = 7.2432e16 FLOPs for one epoch over ~469.6M measured tokens, 1.03-3.58 T4-hours at 10-30% MFU, fitting one free 12-hour session with room for three epochs at the pessimistic MFU. The published points 8.3M and 28M bracket 25.7M. THE GRADING IS THE CATCH AND IT HAS A FREE SUBSTITUTE: GPT-4 grading is 500 calls at $0.68-$8.03, but arXiv:2305.07759 Section 3.1 uses held-out cross-entropy on TinyStories-valid.txt as its own proxy -- qualitative correlation only, no regression, so it cannot be converted into a graded score and must be reported as loss, not as a score. BabyLM/BLiMP is the WEAKER successor for this model: strict-small is 8.4-10.1x too small for a Chinchilla budget at 25.7M, so the right track is Strict (98.04M words), and the honest target is Transformer-XL's 53 on sentential_negation_npi_scope, not GPT-2's 73 and certainly not the 95 my brief carried.

text: it.0 METHODS.md written. SUPERMARTINGALE PROPERTY HOLDS for the grid mixture — proven two ways in §2. Direct: conditional expectation is linear over a finite sum, each term is a single-lambda supermartingale, w_k>=0 preserves each inequality. Reframe: the mixture IS a single predictable-lambda process with lambar_{t-1} = posterior mean of lambda; Ebar_t = Prod(1 + lambar_{i-1} d_i/B) exactly. Not an extension of the predictable-lambda result, a SPECIAL CASE of it. Ville threshold 20 = 1/0.05 exactly. §1.4 repair is NOT fiction.

it.0 BUT THE CONSTRUCTION HAS A LIVE BREAK, and it is B. d_i = NRMSE_twin - NRMSE_settled. NRMSE = RMSE/std(y) is UNBOUNDED ABOVE. Repo record: 2.1166 at n_train=128 and 1.3165 at 512 (CHECKLIST.md:333), seed-mean 1.007076 at 2048 (CHECKLIST.md:868), 5.8198 OOD (ceq/nash.py:4). B=1.0 from the absolute bar is WRONG — the 1.0 bar is a CREDIT rule on the SEED-MEAN at the end, it bounds no individual arm. If |d_i|>B ever occurs a factor goes NEGATIVE, nonnegativity dies, Ville does not apply, every anytime-valid claim in the round is VOID — and the printout looks normal.

it.0 RULE 5 REROUTE for B. Clipping d_i post-hoc does NOT repair it — clipping d up at -B raises the conditional mean and H0 IS a statement about that mean. Repair that works: clip the OUTCOME in the DEFINITION, before any data. d_i = min(NRMSE_twin,C) - min(NRMSE_settled,C), B=C, recommend C=2.0. Legitimate because it defines a new bounded outcome variable a priori; min(.,C) is monotone so per-seed sign never flips; and the round already refuses credit above 1.0 so the clipped scale and the claimable scale agree everywhere the claim may live. Assertion |d_i|<=B must VOID the process, never clamp. Fallback if C not agreed: sign(d_i) in {-1,0,+1}, B=1 — bounded by construction, but discards magnitude and is sprt.py territory.

it.0 THREE MORE CONDITIONS, each invisible in the output when violated. (1) lam_i predictable — automatic under the mixture, which is a reason to prefer it. (2) prior weights w_k CONSTANT — posterior weights move and are supposed to, feeding them back as new priors kills the telescoping identity and there is no theorem left. (3) NO outcome-dependent seed exclusion — dropping a seed for how it came out makes the indicator F_i-measurable not F_{i-1}-measurable and E[I_i d_i|F_{i-1}]<=0 does not follow. The existing NRMSE>=1.0 gate does NOT trip this: it filters CELLS on the seed-mean at the end, not d_i within a cell. Applying the same threshold PER SEED would break the process. Two readings of one number, differing by everything.

it.0 ALPHA BUDGET, unresolved and Chase must pin it before the first seed. Two directions each rejecting at 20 spends alpha=0.05 EACH; two-sided family-wise rate is bounded by 0.10, not 0.05. it.0 FLIESS / CARLYLE-PAZ: **FIELD, NOT COMMUTATIVE RING.** The contract asked and the answer is decisive. Berstel-Reutenauer, Noncommutative Rational Series with Applications, Ch.2 §1: p.27 opens `We start by assuming that K is a commutative ring.` Then p.30, marginal 643, IMMEDIATELY BEFORE the Definition of rank and the Definition of the Hankel matrix: `We suppose from now on that K is a field.` **The hypothesis switches EXACTLY at the definition of rank.** Thm 1.6 (Carlyle and Paz 1971, Fliess 1974a) p.31 verbatim: `The rank of a formal series S is equal to the codimension of its syntactic right ideal, and is equal to the rank of its Hankel matrix.` — carries NO hypothesis of its own, INHERITS the field. Confirmed independently: Balle-Mohri CAI 2015 Thm 1 (Fliess) verbatim `Let S be a field. Then, the rank of the Hankel matrix Hf associated to a function f : Sigma* -> S is finite if and only if f is rational. In that case, there exists a WFA A representing f with rank(Hf) states and no WFA representing f admits fewer states.` Their §3 preamble: `From here on, we will assume that the semiring S is in fact a field. This enables us to define the rank of a matrix.`

it.0 HOW FAR IT ACTUALLY GENERALISES, and it is sideways not upward. NOT to commutative rings — to DIVISION rings. Sakarovitch, Handbook of Weighted Automata Ch.4 draft 19-Sep-2008, §5.2 p.50 verbatim: `We now suppose that K is a field, not necessarily commutative, hence a skew field, or division ring.` Thm 15 p.50: `A series s over A* with coefficients in a division ring is recognisable if and only its rank is finite.` (sic, `if and only its`). OVER SEMIRINGS RANK IS REPLACED, not weakened: Berstel-Reutenauer Ch.1 Prop 5.1 p.11 uses `stable finitely generated left K-submodule` instead, and the Notes p.25 say verbatim `taken from Jacob (1975) who extends to semirings a Hankel-like property given by Fliess (1974a) for fields.` Labai-Makowsky arXiv:1512.02430 §4 p.6 verbatim: `notions of orthogonality, rank, and norms do not readily transfer to the semiring setting.`

it.0 AND THE PID CASE IS AN OPEN PROBLEM, stated as such in print. Berstel-Reutenauer Ch.7 §1 p.121, Thm 1.1 (Fliess 1974a), hypothesis `Let K be a commutative principal ring and let F be its quotient field` — verbatim `Let S in K<<A>> be a series which is rational of rank n over F. Then S is rational over K and has a linear representation over K of dimension n.` NOTE: **the rank is taken over the QUOTIENT FIELD F, then realised over K.** Load-bearing proof step p.122: `mu(K<A>) is a submodule of a free K-module of rank n, hence is also free and has rank <= n` — that is submodule-of-free-is-free, which needs a PID and FAILS over a general commutative ring. And van Heerdt/Kupke/Rot/Silva, FoSSaCS 2020, arXiv:1911.04404v2 p.16 verbatim: `The second part of Lemma 23 would follow from a PID variant of Fliess' theorem [12]. **We are not aware of such a result, and leave this for future work.**` Also Berstel-Reutenauer Ex 5.5 p.24: S = Sum n*a^n IS recognizable over N but the smallest stable N-submodule is NOT finitely generated.

Ville 1939 REACHED IN FULL (numdam.org, Etude critique de la notion de collectif, Gauthier-Villars). **THEOREME 1, printed p.84, verbatim: `Soit {s_n} une suite definissant une martingale et lambda un nombre > 1. Nous avons l inegalite Pr. { B. sup._(n) s_n(X_1, X_2, ..., X_n) >= lambda } <= 1/lambda.`** HYPOTHESIS AS PRINTED: his condition (14) is `s_0 = 1` AND a conditional-expectation **EQUALITY** — a MARTINGALE, not a supermartingale — and lambda > 1. So the form this round uses (SUPERmartingale, E[M_0] <= 1) is NOT Ville 1939 Theoreme 1 verbatim. The supermartingale form is Wang-Ramdas arXiv:2304.01163v3 §2.1 p.4 eq.(3) `P[sup_{0<=n<inf} M_n >= C] <= C^{-1} E[M_0]`, and Durrett V5 Exercise 4.8.2 `P(sup X_n > lambda) <= EX_0/lambda`. METHODS.md now cites the modern form and says why. My §1 proof is self-contained optional stopping so it never depended on the citation.
